subject: Climate & Environment
title: Sulfur Dioxide and Health
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sulfur Dioxide and Health.

hook.text: Sulfur dioxide smells like a struck match. In high doses, it chokes entire cities.

buildup.text: Coal-burning power plants are the biggest source. Volcanoes add more naturally.

discovery.text: SO₂ tightens airways within minutes. Asthmatics are especially sensitive.

twist.text: In the atmosphere, SO₂ turns into sulfate aerosols that actually reflect sunlight and cool Earth.

climax.text: Cleaning up SO₂ saves millions of lives but removes a tiny bit of accidental cooling.

punchline.text: A pollutant that kills people also accidentally cools the planet.

quiz.question: What unexpected effect do sulfate aerosols have?
options: They reflect sunlight and cool Earth slightly

details.summary: Sulfur dioxide is a sharp-smelling gas released primarily by burning coal and oil in power plants and industrial facilities. It aggravates asthma, forms sulfuric acid in the atmosphere, and was the principal pollutant behind historic smog disasters.
details.whyItMatters: SO2 regulations drove some of the earliest clean-air successes. Understanding it shows how policy can dramatically cut pollution when the science is clear.
takeaways: Coal-fired power plants are the largest source of SO2
Even brief exposure can trigger asthma attacks
Cap-and-trade programs cut US SO2 emissions by over 90 percent

faq.question: How did cap-and-trade reduce sulfur dioxide emissions?
faq.answer: The US Acid Rain Program set a total emissions cap and issued tradable allowances. Plants that cut emissions cheaply could sell permits to others, achieving the target at the lowest overall cost and cutting SO2 by over 90 percent since 1990.

faq.question: What health effects does sulfur dioxide cause?
faq.answer: Short-term exposure constricts airways and triggers asthma attacks. Long-term exposure contributes to chronic bronchitis and increases hospital admissions for respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, especially in children and the elderly.
